title: Knowledge Check 5 - Lessons 21-25
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 21-25 - FlexCards | OmniScripts. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A FlexCard displays three fields, but its data source returns a wide record with dozens of fields. What best practice is violated?
options: The theme is wrong
The data source is not lean, adding payload and render cost
The card has too few elements
The output variables are not mapped
questions.explanation: A best practice is to return only the fields the card uses, because extra fields add payload and render cost. The theme, element count, and output variables are not the issue; the data source is over-fetching.

questions.question: An architect nests many child cards when a single flat card would display the same data. What is the primary concern?
options: The card renders too fast
Each child adds render and data-fetch cost, slowing the card
The theme changes
The data source is too lean
questions.explanation: Each child FlexCard is a separate instance with its own render and data-fetch cost, so over-nesting slows the card. Render speed, theme, and a lean data source are not the concern; the nesting itself is.

questions.question: A FlexCard works in the editor but fails in production with empty data. What best practice was most likely skipped?
options: Testing the card in its real placement with real data
Choosing a theme
Adding more elements
Using a chart
questions.explanation: A card can fail in production because of input mapping, missing fields, or placement context, so testing in the target environment with real data is a best practice. Theme, element count, and charts do not address production failures.

questions.question: In a record-centric scenario, a card on a record page shows a small set of fields and offers in-context actions. Which data source is the most appropriate?
options: Integration Procedure
DataRaptor Turbo Extract
Static JSON
A child FlexCard
questions.explanation: A record-centric card on a record page with a small set of fields is best served by a Turbo Extract, which is fast and returns a flat result set. An Integration Procedure is heavier than needed, static JSON cannot pull live record data, and a child card is a composition choice, not a data source.

questions.question: In a role-based scenario, an architect uses conditional rendering to show different sections by role, but one section never appears. What is the most likely cause?
options: The theme is wrong
The data source does not return the field the condition references
The card has too many elements
The placement is a tab
questions.explanation: A condition on a field the data source does not return evaluates to false, so the section is permanently hidden. The theme, element count, and placement do not cause a hidden section when the referenced field is missing.

questions.question: In a console scenario, an agent works entirely in the console and needs a card that follows the selected record. What is the most appropriate placement?
options: A standalone tab
A record page component
A console view
A utility bar
questions.explanation: A console view embeds the card in the console where the agent works and can follow the selected record, matching the workflow. A tab and a utility bar are not tied to the console's record context, and a record page component is outside the console.

questions.question: A consultant is designing an OmniScript for a service agent who must verify the account, then optionally update contact details, then log the interaction. The account verification must always run first. What is the correct Step structure?
options: One Step containing all fields, with the update and log as conditional Elements
Three Steps: verify account, update contact details, log interaction, with the update Step conditional
Two Steps: verify account, then a combined update-and-log Step
A single Step with a branching condition that skips verification when the account is already verified
questions.explanation: The journey is three distinct user intents, so three Steps match it. The update Step is conditional because the agent may not need to change contact details, while verification and logging always run. One combined Step forces unrelated work together, and skipping verification violates the process requirement that it always run first.

questions.question: A conditional Element must appear only when a customer type field equals 'Enterprise'. The field is captured in the same Step, just before the conditional Element. Why might the Element fail to appear?
options: The condition references the wrong JSON path for the customer type field
The Step is marked read-only
The Element has no label
The OmniScript has no translation set
questions.explanation: Conditions evaluate against the data JSON, so the expression must reference the exact path where the customer type value is stored. A wrong path evaluates to empty and the condition is false. Read-only Steps, missing labels, and missing translations do not prevent an Element from rendering.

questions.question: A consultant wants the OmniScript to display in Spanish for users whose locale is set to Spanish. Where is the language selection handled?
options: In the OmniScript's global settings, one language for the whole script
Per Element, with the runtime picking the language from the user's locale or a data JSON value
In the Data Mapper that saves the results
In the Integration Procedure that fetches the account
questions.explanation: Multi-language support is configured per Element, and the runtime selects the language from the user's locale or a language value in the data JSON. There is no single global language switch for the whole script, and Data Mappers and Integration Procedures do not control display language.

questions.question: An OmniScript has a 'business or consumer' choice in the first Step. The rest of the flow differs entirely between the two. What is the cleanest branching design?
options: Make every later Element conditional on the choice, one condition each
Make the two divergent phases conditional Steps, each gated on the choice value
Duplicate the whole OmniScript into two versions
Use a Data Mapper to decide the path
questions.explanation: When an entire phase differs, a conditional Step is the right granularity: one condition hides or shows the whole Step. Making every Element conditional creates many hard-to-maintain conditions, duplicating the OmniScript doubles maintenance, and a Data Mapper does not control UI branching.

questions.question: A branch condition references a field that is captured in a Step that comes after the branch point. What is the result?
options: The branch always triggers
The branch never triggers because the field is empty when the condition evaluates
The OmniScript fails to save
The branch triggers only for the first user
questions.explanation: Conditions evaluate against the data JSON at render time. If the source field is captured later, it is still empty when the condition evaluates, so the branch never triggers. The fix is to capture the decision value before the branch point.

questions.question: A consultant adds a new branch for a rarely used customer type. What must be done for multi-language support?
options: Nothing, translations are inherited from the parent Step
Add a translation for every Element on the new branch for every supported locale
Add one translation for the whole branch
Set the branch to English only
questions.explanation: Multi-language support is per Element, so every Element on the new branch needs a translation for every supported locale. There is no branch-level translation and no inheritance that covers new Elements.

questions.question: An OmniScript must save a single Account record, renaming a few fields from the data JSON to the Account object. What is the appropriate tool?
options: An Integration Procedure that calls a REST service
A Data Mapper that maps the data JSON fields to the Account object
A child OmniScript
A FlexCard
questions.explanation: A single-object save with field renames is deterministic, declarative transform work, which is exactly what a Data Mapper does. An IP is for multi-step or multi-system orchestration, a child OmniScript is for reuse of a sub-journey, and a FlexCard is a display component.

questions.question: An OmniScript must fetch data from an external REST service, transform the response, and merge it with Salesforce data before showing it to the user. What is the appropriate tool?
options: A Data Mapper
An Integration Procedure that orchestrates the REST call, transform, and merge
A formula Element
A validation rule
questions.explanation: This is multi-step orchestration spanning an external system and Salesforce, which is an Integration Procedure's job. A Data Mapper only transforms one structure to another, a formula computes a value, and a validation rule checks input.

questions.question: A consultant is deciding whether to save an OmniScript's data incrementally per Step or once at the end. The journey is long and users frequently abandon mid-way. What is the better choice and why?
options: Save once at the end, because it keeps the record atomic
Save incrementally per Step, because it protects against losing all work on abandonment
Never save, use a Data Mapper only
Save in a child OmniScript
questions.explanation: For a long journey with frequent abandonment, incremental saves protect the work already entered, so a partial record exists even if the user leaves. A single end save risks losing everything on abandonment. The choice is driven by the business outcome, and here the abandonment risk favors incremental saves.
